settings.name: Shape
options: Terminal (text characters, see the Terminal section)
Polar Bloom (Radial as one filled shape)
VU Needles (two analog meters, L and R)
Particles (bars plus sparks on each beat)
Glass Frame (a liquid glass loop round the screen's edges, see Glass Frame)
settings.tip:
The kind of picture the visualizer draws. Changes the whole visualizer.
Stereo: bars growing up from a line.
Mountain: the bars joined into one filled ridge.
Mirror: bars growing both ways from a centre line.
Wave: a smooth curve through the bar tops.
Breathe: one soft shape that swells with the level.
Dots: a dot at each bar's top instead of a bar.
Radial: bars around a circle.
Oscilloscope: the sound's actual waveform as a line, like a lab scope.
Goniometer: a stereo cloud showing how wide the mix is.
Terminal: the spectrum drawn in text characters.
LED Meter: segmented bars, green, amber, red.
Line Spectrum: a filled curve with a glowing edge.
Polar Bloom: Radial drawn as one filled flower.
Spectrogram: a scrolling colour history of the spectrum.
VU Needles: two analog meters, left and right.
Stereo Field: left channel above the line, right below.
Particles: bars plus sparks that fly off on each beat.
Try: Oscilloscope for a thin glowing wave, Stereo for classic bars, Particles for a lively beat-driven look.

settings.name: Reflection
settings.tip:
A faded mirror image of the bars on a floor under them. Shows below the visualizer, only with bars that grow up from the bottom.
Try: 40 for a glossy floor, 100 for a full reflection.

settings.name: Glow
settings.tip:
A soft light around every bar, dot or line. Makes the visualizer itself glow.
Try: 30 for a neon look, 5 for a faint edge glow.

settings.name: Glow Radius
settings.tip:
How far the glow reaches out from each bar. Only matters with Glow above 0.
Try: 3 for a tight halo, 12 for a hazy one.

settings.name: Bloom
settings.tip:
Light bleeding out of the whole picture, like a camera lens catching something bright. Spreads past the bars onto the panel.
Try: 15 for a dreamy shine, 50 for a strong blown-out look.

settings.name: Bloom Radius
settings.tip:
How far the bloom light spreads. Only matters with Bloom above 0.
Try: 4 for a close shine, 24 for a wide wash.

settings.name: Outline Width
settings.tip:
A thin line just inside each bar's edge. Bars keep their size.
Try: 1 with a white Outline Color for crisp, drawn-looking bars.

settings.name: Outline Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the bar outline. Only shows with Outline Width above 0.
Try: #B0FFFFFF for a soft white edge.

settings.name: Shadow
settings.tip:
A drop shadow behind every bar, dot and line, falling on the panel or wallpaper.
Try: 50 to lift the bars off a busy wallpaper.

settings.name: Shadow Color
settings.tip:
The shadow's colour.
Try: #000000 for a normal shadow, your accent colour for a coloured echo.

settings.name: Shadow Offset X
settings.tip:
How far the shadow sits to the right of the bars (negative is left).
Try: 2 for a subtle offset, 0 for a shadow straight below.

settings.name: Shadow Offset Y
settings.tip:
How far the shadow sits below the bars (negative is above).
Try: 3 for a light-from-above look.

settings.name: Shadow Softness
settings.tip:
How blurry the shadow's edge is. 0 is a hard, flat shadow.
Try: 0 for a retro pixel shadow, 6 for a soft one.

settings.name: Hollow Bars
settings.tip:
Draws bars as outlines with the inside left see-through.
Try: On with Hollow Line Width 1.5 for a wireframe look.

settings.name: Hollow Line Width
settings.tip:
How thick the outline of a hollow bar is. Only with Hollow Bars on.
Try: 1 for hairlines, 3 for bold outlines.

settings.name: Dash Length
settings.tip:
Cuts every bar into dashes along its length, like an LED segment meter. 0 keeps bars solid.
Try: 2 with Dash Gap 1 for a dotted meter look.

settings.name: Dash Gap
settings.tip:
The space between the dashes. Only with Dash Length above 0.
Try: 1 for tight segments, 3 for open ones.

settings.name: Tilt
settings.tip:
Leans every bar sideways from its base, like italic text.
Try: 15 for a sense of speed, -15 to lean the other way.

settings.name: Mirror Gap
settings.tip:
With Anchor set to Middle, pulls the top and bottom halves of the bars apart, leaving a spine.
Try: 2 for a thin centre line through the bars.

settings.name: Afterimage
settings.tip:
A see-through trail behind each bar that jumps up with it and sinks back slowly.
Try: 25 for a ghostly echo of every hit.

settings.name: Afterimage Length
settings.tip:
How many seconds the afterimage trail takes to sink away. Only with Afterimage above 0.
Try: 1.75 for a slow fade, 0.5 for a quick flicker.

settings.name: Orientation
settings.tip:
Which way the visualizer runs.
Horizontal: bars side by side across the screen, growing up (or down).
Vertical: bars stacked down the screen, growing sideways, to stand along a screen edge.
Try: Vertical beside a window or along the side of the screen.

settings.name: Bar Count
settings.tip:
How many bars are drawn across the visualizer. More bars means more detail and thinner spacing.
Try: 32 for chunky bars, 135 for a fine, detailed spectrum.

settings.name: Bar Width
settings.tip:
How thick each bar is, in pixels.
Try: 2 for a fine line look, 8 for bold blocks.

settings.name: Bar Gap
settings.tip:
The space between bars, in pixels.
Try: 1 for a near-solid wall, 4 for clearly separate bars.

settings.name: Bar Max Size
settings.tip:
How tall a bar can get at full volume, in pixels. Sets the visualizer's height.
Try: 18 for a slim strip, 140 for a tall display.

settings.name: Bar Idle Size
settings.tip:
The height bars keep when nothing is playing, so it never goes fully flat. -1 hides them.
Try: 2 for a resting line, -1 to vanish in silence.

settings.name: Bar Corner Radius
settings.tip:
How round the bar corners are. One number for all, or four for each corner.
Try: 0 for square pixel bars, 3 for soft pills.

settings.name: Color Mode
settings.tip:
Where the bar colours come from.
Solid: every bar in Color.
Gradient: a fade from Gradient Color 1 on the left to 2 on the right.
Reactive Gradient: each bar picks between the two by how loud it is (quiet = 1, loud = 2).
Windows Accent Color: your Windows accent colour.
Album Art Color: the main colour of the playing song's cover.
Dynamic Album Gradient: a gradient made from the cover's colours.
Acrylic: see-through frosted bars tinted with Color.
Rainbow Cycle: colours that keep cycling (speed below).
Tourne: the Tourne teal-to-red fade.
Try: Reactive Gradient so loud hits change colour, Album Art Color to match each song.

settings.name: Color
settings.tip:
The bar colour when Color Mode is Solid (and the tint for Acrylic).
Try: your palette red #E57474, or #15FFA2 for neon green.

settings.name: Gradient Color 1
settings.tip:
The first colour of the gradient (left, or the quiet end for Reactive Gradient).
Try: #4CE38D for a green-to-red Tourne fade.

settings.name: Gradient Color 2
settings.tip:
The second colour of the gradient (right, or the loud end for Reactive Gradient).
Try: #A95D5D to end the fade in a muted red.

settings.name: Sensitivity
settings.tip:
How strongly the bars react to sound. Higher fills the bars with quieter music.
Try: 100 for a calm look, 200 if bars barely move.

settings.name: Sensitivity Curve
settings.tip:
What happens when a loud sound would push a bar past the top.
Exponential (Soft): squeezes early and smoothly; loud parts look gentle and nothing slams the ceiling, but big hits look smaller.
Knee (Balanced): leaves quiet and medium levels exactly as they are and only squeezes the loudest part; the usual choice.
Power (Headroom): squeezes least and latest, so hits stay punchy and bars reach the top more often.
Try: Knee for most music, Power for punchy electronic, Exponential for calm, smooth motion.

settings.name: Input Gain (dB)
settings.tip:
A fixed volume boost or cut on the sound before the visualizer reads it, in dB.
Try: 3 if your player volume is low, -3 if everything maxes out.

settings.name: Auto Gain
settings.tip:
Lifts quiet sources automatically so they still fill the bars. Loud music is unchanged.
Try: On if you switch between quiet podcasts and loud music.

settings.name: Auto Gain Max Boost (dB)
settings.tip:
The most Auto Gain is allowed to lift a quiet sound, in dB.
Try: 9 for gentle help, 18 for very quiet sources.

settings.name: Motion Smoothing
settings.tip:
Makes bars rise and fall more slowly for a steadier, calmer motion.
Try: 0 for snappy, 6 for smooth and easy to watch.

settings.name: EQ Preset
settings.tip:
Boosts parts of the sound before it's drawn, to suit a music style.
Default: no change.
Bass: lifts the low end, for hip-hop and EDM.
Rock: lifts lows and highs a little, mids flat.
Pop: lifts vocals and mids.
Jazz: gentle lift to mids and highs.
Electronic: lifts sub-bass and treble.
Try: Default for an honest view, Bass if your music is bass-heavy but the left bars look flat.

settings.name: FFT Size
settings.tip:
How finely the sound is split into pitches before it becomes bars.
1024: fastest reaction, least detail (bass bars blur together).
2048: the balance; the sweet spot with the Precision engine.
4096: more detail in the bass, a touch slower.
8192: the most detail, slightly laggier and more CPU.
Try: 2048 for most setups, 8192 for many thin bars on a big screen.

settings.name: Frequency Scale
options: ERB (auditory filter bandwidths, Glasberg and Moore)
settings.tip:
How bars are spread from low to high pitch.
Log: each octave gets equal room, like a piano; the natural look.
Linear: equal Hz per bar; bass squashed into a few bars on the left, treble takes most of the width.
Mel: spaced like the pitches we hear as evenly spaced.
Bark: spaced like the ear's critical bands; more room for the mids.
ERB: spaced like the ear's own filters; a balanced, ear-like spread.
Try: Log for music, ERB for an evenly busy spectrum.

settings.name: Peak Frequency Readout
settings.tip:
Shows a small number with the strongest pitch right now (or loudness, see Readout Content), near the bars.
Try: On with the Terminal font for a studio meter look.

settings.name: Peak Readout - Horizontal Position
settings.tip:
Where the readout sits from left to right.
Left, Center or Right of the visualizer.
Try: Right to keep it clear of the bass on the left.

settings.name: Peak Readout - Vertical Position
settings.tip:
Where the readout sits from top to bottom.
Above: outside, over the visualizer.
Top: inside, along the top.
Middle: inside, centred.
Bottom: inside, along the bottom.
Below: outside, under the visualizer.
Try: Above for a clean label that never covers the bars.

settings.name: Multiband Oscilloscope Coloring
settings.tip:
Colours the Oscilloscope line by which part of the sound is strongest: low, mid or high.
Try: On for a scope that changes colour with the music.

settings.name: Oscilloscope Time Window (ms)
settings.tip:
How much time the Oscilloscope line shows end to end. Short looks like a lab scope, long like a rolling wave.
Try: 24 for sharp wave cycles, 175 for a smooth ribbon.

settings.name: Oscilloscope Damping
settings.tip:
Slows how fast the Oscilloscope line changes shape so it is easier to follow.
Try: 0 for raw and jittery, 80 for a slow, flowing line.

settings.name: Anchor
settings.tip:
Where bars grow from.
Bottom: up from a floor, the classic equalizer.
Top: down from a ceiling, like icicles.
Middle: both ways from a centre line, like a waveform.
Try: Middle for a waveform look, Bottom for a classic equalizer.

settings.name: Peak Hold Caps
settings.tip:
Small caps that hang at each bar's recent highest point, then fall.
Try: On with a bright cap colour for a classic hi-fi look.

settings.name: Peak Hold Cap Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the peak caps. Always used, whatever the Color Mode.
Try: #15FFA2 for neon caps over red bars.

settings.name: Beat Flash
settings.tip:
Briefly flashes the bars toward the Beat Flash Color on every bass hit.
Try: On to make kicks pop.

settings.name: Beat Flash Color
settings.tip:
The colour bars flash toward on a beat. Lower its alpha for a gentler tint.
Try: #15FFA2 for a green pulse, #80FFFFFF for a soft white one.

settings.name: Beat Flash Intensity
settings.tip:
How fast and strongly a beat reaches the flash colour.
Try: 80 for a clear flash, 150 for a punchy strobe.

settings.name: Rainbow Cycle Speed
settings.tip:
How fast the colours cycle with Color Mode set to Rainbow.
Try: 20 for a slow drift, 80 for a fast party cycle.

settings.name: Now Playing Text
settings.tip:
Shows the song's artist and title near the visualizer.
Try: On with a pixel font for a retro display.

settings.name: Now Playing Text Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the song title text.
Try: your palette red #E57474.

settings.name: Now Playing Font
settings.tip:
The font for the song text (any installed font).
Try: a pixel font like Delicatus, or Segoe UI for clean text.

settings.name: Now Playing Font Size
settings.tip:
The size of the song text, in points.
Try: 14 for a subtle label, 20 for a headline.

settings.name: Now Playing Display Seconds
settings.tip:
How long the song text stays after a track changes. 0 keeps it on all the time.
Try: 0 for an always-on widget, 6 for a brief pop-up.

settings.name: Now Playing Offset X
settings.tip:
Slides the song text left (negative) or right, in pixels.
Try: small steps like 10 to clear the panel edge.

settings.name: Now Playing Offset Y
settings.tip:
Slides the song text up (negative) or down, in pixels.
Try: -4 to give it a little more room above the bars.

settings.name: Now Playing Background
settings.tip:
A small panel just behind the song text, so it reads over a busy wallpaper. Transparent means none.
Try: #141B1E for a dark label box.

settings.name: Now Playing Background Padding
settings.tip:
The space between the song text and the edge of its panel.
Try: 4 for a snug box, 8 for a roomy one.

settings.name: Now Playing Background Corner Radius
settings.tip:
How round the song text panel's corners are.
Try: 0 for square, 6 for soft.

settings.name: Now Playing Background Border Size
settings.tip:
An outline around the song text panel. 0 is none.
Try: 1 with your accent colour for a framed label.

settings.name: Now Playing Background Border Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the song text panel's outline.
Try: #64AA89 for a muted green frame.

settings.name: Now Playing Backdrop
settings.tip:
What the song text panel shows of the wallpaper behind it, tinted by Now Playing Background. Desktop only.
Try: Acrylic with a background of #60101418.

settings.name: Peak Readout Offset X
settings.tip:
Slides the readout left (negative) or right, in pixels.
Try: small steps like 6 for fine placement.

settings.name: Peak Readout Offset Y
settings.tip:
Slides the readout up (negative) or down, in pixels.
Try: -2 to lift it off the bars.

settings.name: Peak Readout Background
settings.tip:
A small panel just behind the readout so it reads over the bars. Transparent means none.
Try: #141B1E for a dark tag.

settings.name: Peak Readout Background Padding
settings.tip:
The space between the readout and the edge of its panel.
Try: 4.

settings.name: Peak Readout Background Corner Radius
settings.tip:
How round the readout panel's corners are.
Try: 0 for square, 6 for soft.

settings.name: Peak Readout Background Border Size
settings.tip:
An outline around the readout panel. 0 is none.
Try: 1 for a framed tag.

settings.name: Peak Readout Background Border Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the readout panel's outline.
Try: #64AA89.

settings.name: Now Playing Layout
settings.tip:
How the song text is laid out.
One line: "Artist - Title".
Two lines: the title, with the artist under it in its own colour.
Try: Two lines for a media-card feel.

settings.name: Now Playing Placement
settings.tip:
Where the song text goes.
Above the visualizer: over the panel, outside it.
Inside the panel, top: in the panel's padding above the bars.
Inside the panel, bottom: in the padding below them (give the panel enough padding on that side).
Try: Inside the panel, top, with 20 top padding for a tidy widget.

settings.name: Now Playing Alignment
settings.tip:
Lines the song text up on the left, in the centre, or on the right of the bars.
Try: Left to line it up with the first bar.

settings.name: Now Playing Artist Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the artist part of the song text.
Try: #64AA89 to set the artist apart from the title.

settings.name: Text Rendering
settings.tip:
How the song text, readout and Terminal text are drawn.
Smooth: soft, antialiased edges; right for normal fonts.
Pixel: hard pixels with no smoothing; right for pixel fonts at their design size (or a multiple).
Try: Pixel with a pixel font for crisp retro text.

settings.name: Audio Source
settings.tip:
What the visualizer listens to.
Default output: what you hear, from your speakers or headphones.
Default input: your microphone or line-in.
A device by name: any output or input, virtual cables included, named in Device Name.
Try: Default output to follow your music.

settings.name: Device Name
settings.tip:
Part of a device's name to listen to, when Audio Source is a named device.
Try: "CABLE Output" for a virtual cable.

settings.name: Source Boost
settings.tip:
How strongly a device or a program moves the bars, up to 1000%, without changing how loud you hear it: part of its name = a percent, several separated by commas. The rows under it list what is heard and playing now.
Try: "Spotify=400" for one program.

settings.name: Hiss above (Hz)
settings.tip:
The sound above this pitch counts as hiss (cymbals, air, noise), 2000 to 20000.
Try: 8000; 12000 for only the air.

settings.name: Rumble below (Hz)
settings.tip:
The sound below this pitch counts as rumble (sub bass, hum, wind), 20 to 300.
Try: 60; 40 for only the deepest.

settings.name: Quiet below (dB)
settings.tip: A source softer than this is quiet; between this and Loud above, medium. -80 to -10.

settings.name: Loud above (dB)
settings.tip: A source louder than this is loud. -40 to 0.

settings.name: Hiss (dB)
settings.tip:
How much more (up) or less (down: the bars see less of it) of every source's hiss moves the bars, -24 to +24. Your sound is untouched.
A source's own: in Source Boost after its percent, e.g. "Spotify=100 hiss:-6".

settings.name: Rumble (dB)
settings.tip: The same for the rumble, -24 to +24 (a source's own: rumble:+6).

settings.name: Quiet (dB)
settings.tip:
How much a source moves the bars while it's quiet, -24 to +24 (a source's own: quiet:+12).
Try: +10 so soft passages still show.

settings.name: Medium (dB)
settings.tip: The same at medium volume (a source's own: medium:0).

settings.name: Loud (dB)
settings.tip:
The same while it's loud, -24 to +24 (a source's own: loud:-6).
Try: -6 so loud parts don't pin the bars.

settings.name: Bands
settings.tip: The bands made in Tune by ear (right-click > Audio Source > Tune by ear, or the panel's Audio Source page): type, Hz, dB, Q, on.

settings.name: Bars See the Curve
settings.tip: The bands shape what the visualizer sees, for every source. Your sound is untouched.

settings.name: Tone Level (dB)
settings.tip:
How loud the tone plays, -60 to -12 (never louder than -12).
Try: -30, and your volume low.

settings.name: Tone Fade (ms)
settings.tip: How long the tone fades in and out, so it never clicks. 5 to 500.

settings.name: Tone Glide (ms)
settings.tip:
How quickly the pitch follows the drag, so a sweep sounds smooth. 1 to 200.
Try: 8.

settings.name: Lyrics
settings.tip: The playing song's words, timed to the music. Off by default. Found in your folder, or online if you allow it below.

settings.name: Lyrics Folder
settings.tip:
A folder of .lrc files named "Artist - Title.lrc" or "Title.lrc". Looked in first; needs no network.
Try: the folder your music player saves lyrics to.

settings.name: Look Up Online
settings.tip: Asks lrclib.net for lyrics your folder doesn't have. Sends only the song's artist, title and album, as "TourneTable"; nothing about you or this PC. Each song is asked for once, then kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tourne\Lyrics.

settings.name: lrclib, Looser Search
settings.tip: When lrclib.net has no exact match, asks it again with a looser search (artist and title as one phrase) and takes the closest title, artist and length. Sends the artist and title, as "TourneTable"; nothing else.

settings.name: NetEase
settings.tip: Asks NetEase Cloud Music (music.163.com), which has timed lyrics for many songs, Chinese and Western. Sends the artist and title, as "TourneTable"; nothing else.

settings.name: Genius
settings.tip: Asks Genius's search with your access token below, then reads the words off the song's Genius web page (that page is outside Genius's API, and Genius sometimes refuses it). Genius's words are untimed: see Untimed Lyrics. Sends the artist and title; the token goes only to api.genius.com.

settings.name: Genius Access Token
settings.tip: Your own, from genius.com/api-clients (Generate Access Token). Kept with your other settings; never written to a log.

settings.name: My Own Site
settings.tip: Asks the address below with the song filled in. It should answer with .lrc or plain text; markup is stripped and nothing in it is followed.

settings.name: My Own Site's Address
settings.tip:
With {artist}, {title}, {album} and {length} (seconds) in it.
Try: https://example.com/lyrics?a={artist}&t={title}

settings.name: Fix Names with Last.fm
settings.tip: Before looking anywhere online, asks Last.fm for the right spelling of the artist and title (with your API key below), so a misspelt tag still finds its lyrics. Sends the artist and title.

settings.name: Last.fm API Key
settings.tip: Your own, from last.fm/api. Kept with your other settings; never written to a log.

settings.name: Untimed Lyrics
settings.tip: Lyrics without times (Genius, many plain files): spread evenly across the song, with your animation; shown as a still block that moves on a line at a time with no animation; or not shown.

settings.name: Translate Lyrics
settings.tip: A translation of the words into your language, made by people, never by a machine: your own files, and NetEase's and Genius's translators, each with its own switch below. When none is found, the words show as they are, with nothing in their place. Also in the lines' right-click menu.

settings.name: Language
settings.tip:
A language code. Empty: Windows' display language.
Try: en, es, de, fr, it, pt, ru, ja, ko, zh (the right-click menu lists more).

settings.name: Show
settings.tip: The translation alongside the words, or alone in their place (with the lines' times; the word times are the original's, so Karaoke fills by line).

settings.name: Place
settings.tip: Where the translation goes, with Original and translation: under or above each line, or its own block with its own place, dragged as the lyrics are (when unlocked below). Web animations (engine = web) show the original only for now.

settings.name: Block Across (%)
settings.tip: With Its own block: where its middle is, across the screen, 0 to 100. Dragging it sets this.

settings.name: Block Down (%)
settings.tip: With Its own block: where its middle is, down the screen, 0 to 100. -1: just under the lyrics, wherever they are. Dragging it sets this.

settings.name: Block Locked
settings.tip: With Its own block: it stays put. Off, drag it with the lyrics' drag button and key. Also in the right-click menu.

settings.name: Its Own Look
settings.tip: Off: the translation takes the lyrics' font and colours (sung, other lines), smaller. On: the font, colour and opacity below.

settings.name: Font
settings.tip: Any installed font's name, with Its own look. Empty: the lyrics' font.

settings.name: Size (%)
settings.tip: Of the lyrics' text size, 30 to 150.

settings.name: Colour
settings.tip: With Its own look.

settings.name: Opacity (%)
settings.tip: With Its own look, 0 to 100.

settings.name: From Your Files
settings.tip: "Artist - Title.<language>.lrc" (or "Title.<language>.lrc") in the Lyrics Folder, timed or not: for example "Artist - Title.en.lrc". Needs no network.

settings.name: From NetEase
settings.tip: NetEase Cloud Music's translated lyrics, made by its listeners, timed with the song. Used only when they're in your language: most are Chinese, a few English. Sends the artist and title.

settings.name: From Genius
settings.tip: Genius's translation pages, written by its translators (Genius English Translations and the others), with your Genius Access Token. Untimed: laid line for line, and only used when the line counts agree. Sends the artist, title and language.

settings.name: From a Model on This PC
settings.tip:
Machine translation into English, by a small model on this PC picked by the language of the words (one folder per language pair in the Translation Models Folder, so you add only the languages you want). Tried after every translation made by people, and always marked on screen as machine translation. Needs no network.
Try: on, with a model for the languages you listen to.

settings.name: Translation Drawn
settings.tip:
Like the lyrics: the translation takes the lyrics' animation in and out, glow, beat pop and flash, the sung colour (spread over the line, as translations have no word times) and Depth's cut-out, under, above or in its own block. Has Its Own Look still sets its font, colour and opacity. Plain: a fade with its line, as before.
Try: Like the lyrics.

settings.name: Translation Animation
settings.tip:
With Translation Drawn: Like the lyrics, how the translation's lines come in and go: the lyrics' own animation, or one of its own.
Try: Same as the lyrics, or Fade for a calmer translation.

settings.name: Translation Glow
settings.tip:
The lyrics' glow on the translation too, or none on it.
Try: Same as the lyrics.

settings.name: Translation Beat Pop and Flash
settings.tip:
The lyrics' beat pop and flash on the translation too, or the translation kept still.
Try: Off, if the translation is hard to read.

settings.name: Translation Sung Colour
settings.tip:
The sung colour across the translation over the original line's time (it has no word times of its own), or the playing translation all in the sung colour.
Try: Sweeps like the lyrics.

settings.name: Translation Depth
settings.tip:
With the lyrics behind the wallpaper's cut-out subject: the translation behind it too, or always in front so it stays readable.
Try: Same as the lyrics.

settings.name: Machine Translation Note
settings.tip:
A small "Machine translation" line under the lyrics when what's shown was put into English by a model or by listening. Show Where It's From governs the other sources' lines. A model that's there but can't run is said either way.
Try: on.

settings.name: Translation Models Folder
settings.tip: Where the translation models are, one folder each named for its pair, like opus-mt-ru-en: an OPUS-MT model in ONNX form (encoder and decoder .onnx, source.spm, vocab.json, config.json). Empty: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tourne\Table\Models\Translate.

settings.name: By Listening
settings.tip:
For timed lyrics nothing above could translate: what's sung is heard from the sound the Table already takes and put into English by whisper.cpp, line by line, a few seconds behind the singing. Always marked on screen as machine translation (heard). Needs no network; uses up to three cores while a song wants it, nothing otherwise.
Try: on, for songs in languages you have no text model for.

settings.name: Listening Models Folder
settings.tip: Where whisper.dll and its many-language ggml model (ggml-small.bin or similar) are. Empty: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tourne\Table\Models\Listen.

settings.name: ONNX Runtime Folder
settings.tip: The folder with onnxruntime.dll (64-bit, 1.17 or newer) that runs the models. Empty: Tourne Desktop's own, else the models folder.

settings.name: Show Where It's From
settings.tip: A small line under the lyrics: Translation: NetEase, Genius, your file.

settings.name: Timing Offset (ms)
settings.tip:
Moves the words earlier (minus) or later (plus) against the music, -5000 to 5000.
Try: -200 if they come in late.

settings.name: Animation
settings.tip:
How each line comes in, is sung and goes. Ours move whole words or letters; the living wallpapers' swap letters as they do there (Bonsai's message, Departures' board, Prompt's terminal).
Try: Decode, or Karaoke with a word-timed file.

settings.name: Fill Follows the Singer
settings.tip:
The sung colour (Karaoke and the other filling animations) sweeps on with the singer: each word starts filling at its own time, from word-timed lyrics, or when it's heard starting in the music (Word Pop's Onset rows), and fills at the pace being sung, so a drawn-out word fills slowly and holds short of its end until the next word begins, and a short one fills at once. With nothing heard, the line's time is shared out by syllables. Off: an even spread over the line, as before.
Try: on.

settings.name: Fill Lead (ms)
settings.tip:
How far ahead of the word the fill runs, to make up for the moment it takes to hear a sound start. The Timing offset still moves everything.
Try: 60; more if the colour still trails the voice.

settings.name: Pace With the Song
settings.tip:
The chosen animation's read-in sped up or slowed down by how fast the words are sung (and a little by loudness), so each word, or each letter for the letter-by-letter ones, has finished appearing just before it's sung: fast passages read out faster, slow held ones slower. With word-timed lyrics it lands ahead of each word; with lyrics timed per line it paces across the line's known start and end. Leaving lines and Disperse keep their own lengths. Off, every animation runs at its own length. Also in the lines' right-click menu under Animation.
Try: on, with Decode or Typewriter.

settings.name: Arrive Ahead (ms)
settings.tip: How long before a word is sung its read-in finishes. 30 is about four frames at 144 Hz; 0 exactly on the word.

settings.name: Pace Fastest (%)
settings.tip: The quickest the read-in may run, as a share of the animation's own length, so it never looks frantic.

settings.name: Pace Slowest (%)
settings.tip: The slowest the read-in may run, as a share of the animation's own length, so it never looks frozen.

settings.name: Pace Loudness (%)
settings.tip: How much loudness nudges the pace: louder, snappier. Tempo does most of the work. 0 none.

settings.name: Animation File
settings.tip: Your own animation: a text file of key = value lines (unit = line|word|letter; in.ms, in.stagger, in.ease = linear|out|inout|back, in.opacity, in.x, in.y, in.scale; the same for out.; react.beat, react.wave, glow, karaoke, glyph = decode|flip|flap..., glyph.speed). Used when Animation is My animation file.

settings.name: Font
settings.tip:
Any installed font's name.
Try: CozetteVector for the pixel look.

settings.name: Text Size (px)
settings.tip: How big the words are, 10 to 160 (at 100% scaling).

settings.name: Across (%)
settings.tip: Where the lines' middle sits across the Table's screen, 0 (left edge) to 100 (right edge).

settings.name: Down (%)
settings.tip:
Where the lines' middle sits down the screen, 0 (top) to 100 (bottom).
Try: 30, above the visualizer.

settings.name: Width (%)
settings.tip: How much of the screen's width the lines may use, 10 to 100. Longer lines are cut at its edges.

settings.name: Align
settings.tip: The lines' alignment in that width.

settings.name: Lines Before
settings.tip: Lines already sung kept above the playing one, 0 to 6.

settings.name: Lines After
settings.tip: Lines still to come shown below it, 0 to 6.

settings.name: Scroll (ms)
settings.tip: How long the stack takes to move up a line when the next one starts, 0 (a jump) to 3000.

settings.name: Sung Colour
settings.tip: The playing line's words once they're sung (all of it when Karaoke is off in your file).

settings.name: Waiting Colour
settings.tip: The playing line's words still to come, and Decode's settling glyphs.

settings.name: Other Lines Colour
settings.tip: The lines before and after the playing one.

settings.name: Lock in Place
settings.tip: The lines can't be dragged. Off: drag them with the visualizer's drag button and key (even with Enable Drag-to-Move off or Lock everything on, which keep the Table's other parts in place), and the place you drop them lands in Across and Down. Also in the lines' right-click menu, which still opens while they're locked.

settings.name: Instrumental Disperse
settings.tip:
When the song goes instrumental (a long wait to the next line, or an empty timed line), the lines on screen clear away with one of Tourne Desktop's window close effects, letter by letter: Wake (the lines drop, eaten from the top along a glowing edge), Derez (read out from the top into falling code), Shatter (they crack and fall apart), Melt (each letter runs down on its own beat), Dust (swept from the left into drifting specks) or Motion (they shrink a little and fade). The next line reads in with the animation as usual. None: they stay, as before.
Try: Dust.

settings.name: Disperse Length (ms)
settings.tip: How long the clearing away takes, 100 to 5000.

settings.name: Instrumental Gap (s)
settings.tip:
A wait this long or longer to the next line counts as an instrumental stretch, 2 to 120.
Try: 8.

settings.name: Hold Before Dispersing (s)
settings.tip: How long the last line stays before the lines clear, 0 to 60. With word times: counted from its last word, a second at least. An empty timed line clears them at once.

settings.name: Depth
settings.tip:
Behind the cut-out: the lines pass behind the wallpaper's subject, as the bars do with Depth, using the cut-out the Depth page finds or makes (its Source, Fit, Scale and Offset). Works whether or not the bars use Depth; the lyrics' own choice. In front: as before.
Try: Behind, with lines placed across the subject.

settings.name: Beat pop integration link
settings.tip:
Whose beat settings the lyrics follow, read live so a change there shows here at once. The lyrics' own: Beat Flash and Beat Pop's rows on this page. The bars' Beat Flash (Appearance > Colours): flashes when it's on, in its colour, at its strength; pops at that strength. The Glass Frame's Beat Flash (Glass Frame > Light): its strength, colour and fade, and its Fill as how much the lines round the playing one flash too. Linked, this page's Beat Flash, its colour and strength and Pop Strength and Length follow the link; Beat Pop's switch and Pop Look stay the lyrics' own.
Try: the Glass Frame's, so the words flash with the frame.

settings.name: Beat Pop
settings.tip:
On each beat (the bass hits that drive Beat Flash and the Glass Frame's Bass Glow, with either analysis engine) the playing line gets a short pop, laid over the animation that's running.
Try: On with Emboss.

settings.name: Pop Look
settings.tip: Depress: the words press in (an inset edge). Emboss: they rise (a raised edge). Inverse: their colours flip for the hit. Press: the letters spread from the line's middle and come back, as the cursor's reticle opens on a press.

settings.name: Pop Direction
settings.tip: Out: each look as it is. In: the playing line sinks toward the desktop on the beat, like a button pressed in, and springs back: Emboss shrinks with its edge turned inward, Inverse flips and sinks, Press draws the letters together instead of apart. Depress, already a press, mirrors to rise. Over any animation, and with the Beat pop integration link.

settings.name: Pop Strength (%)
settings.tip: How strong each pop is, 0 to 100.

settings.name: Pop Length (ms)
settings.tip:
How long one pop lasts, in and out, 40 to 2000.
Try: 160 for Press, like the cursor.

settings.name: Word Pop
settings.tip:
Each word pops as it's sung, in Beat Pop's look (Depress, Emboss, Inverse, Press) and Pop Direction, over any animation. Loud music and fast singing make the pops quicker and stronger; slow held words get longer, softer ones. Word times come from word-timed lyrics; otherwise each line's time is shared out by syllables. Also in the lines' right-click menu.
Try: on, with Emboss.

settings.name: Word Pop Strength (%)
settings.tip: How strong each word's pop is, 0 to 100.

settings.name: Word Pop Length (ms)
settings.tip:
How long a word's pop lasts at an even tempo and level; loudness and tempo shorten or lengthen it from here.
Try: 240.

settings.name: Word Pop Shortest (ms)
settings.tip: The quickest a pop may get with fast, loud singing.

settings.name: Word Pop Longest (ms)
settings.tip: The longest a pop may get on slow, quiet words.

settings.name: Word Pop Motion (px)
settings.tip: How far each word rises as it pops (sinks, with Pop In), and settles back. 0 none.

settings.name: Word Pop Fade (%)
settings.tip: How faded a word starts as it pops in, coming up to full as the pop runs. 0 none, 100 from nothing.

settings.name: Scales Speed (%)
settings.tip: How much loudness and tempo change how fast each pop runs. 0 off (always Word Pop Length), 100 as set, 200 double.

settings.name: Scales Fade (%)
settings.tip: How much loudness and tempo change the fade. 0 off, 100 as set, 200 double.

settings.name: Scales Motion (%)
settings.tip: How much loudness and tempo change how far words move. 0 off, 100 as set, 200 double.

settings.name: Scales Strength (%)
settings.tip: How much loudness and tempo change the pop's strength. 0 off, 100 as set, 200 double.

settings.name: Loudness Drive (%)
settings.tip: How much the music's loudness as each word starts drives its pop: louder, quicker and bigger. 0 none.

settings.name: Syllable Tempo Drive (%)
settings.tip: How much the syllables per second being sung drive the pop: fast singing gives quick, short pops; slow held words longer, softer ones. 0 none.

settings.name: Smoothing (%)
settings.tip: How much each word's drive leans on the word before and on the whole line, so neighbouring pops don't jump. 0 each word on its own.

settings.name: Onset Sensitivity (%)
settings.tip:
On songs whose lyrics are timed per line (no word times), the pops follow the music instead of a guess: each sound heard starting (the level jumping above its recent run) moves the pop on to the next word, within the line's own time. Higher hears smaller jumps. With nothing heard (silence), the line's time is shared out by syllables. The lines' right-click menu says which is in use.
Try: 60; higher if words lag, lower if they race ahead.

settings.name: Onset Gap (ms)
settings.tip:
The shortest time between two heard word starts, so one note's ring doesn't count twice.
Try: 110; 160 for slow songs.

settings.name: Shadow (%)
settings.tip:
A soft shadow under the words, as the bars' Shadow. 0 off, 100 solid.
Try: 50.

settings.name: Shadow Colour
settings.tip: The shadow's colour.

settings.name: Shadow Across (px)
settings.tip: How far right the shadow falls (minus: left), -40 to 40.

settings.name: Shadow Down (px)
settings.tip: How far down the shadow falls (minus: up), -40 to 40.

settings.name: Shadow Softness (px)
settings.tip: How blurred the shadow is, 0 (sharp) to 40.

settings.name: Glow (%)
settings.tip:
A soft light round every letter in its own colour, as the bars' Glow. 0 off.
Try: 40 for a neon look.

settings.name: Glow Radius (px)
settings.tip: How far the glow reaches, 1 to 40.

settings.name: Bloom (%)
settings.tip:
Light bleeding wide out of the words, as the bars' Bloom. 0 off.
Try: 25 for a dreamy shine.

settings.name: Bloom Radius (px)
settings.tip: How far the bloom spreads, 2 to 80.

settings.name: Outline (px)
settings.tip:
A line round every letter, 0 (none) to 8.
Try: 1 or 2, in a dark colour, for words that read over any wallpaper.

settings.name: Outline Colour
settings.tip: The outline's colour.

settings.name: Highlight (%)
settings.tip:
A light sheen over the top of the letters, fading down each line. 0 off.
Try: 35.

settings.name: Highlight Colour
settings.tip: The sheen's colour.

settings.name: Beat Flash
settings.tip: The words flash toward the colour below on each beat, as the bars' Beat Flash.

settings.name: Beat Flash Colour
settings.tip: The colour they flash toward.

settings.name: Beat Flash Strength (%)
settings.tip: How far toward that colour, 0 to 100.

settings.name: Background
settings.tip: A panel behind the lines, as the bars' Background.

settings.name: Background Colour
settings.tip: The panel's colour; its alpha is how see-through it is.

settings.name: Background Padding (px)
settings.tip: Room round the words inside the panel, 0 to 80.

settings.name: Corner Radius (px)
settings.tip: How round the panel's corners are, 0 (square) to 80.

settings.name: Border (px)
settings.tip: A line round the panel, 0 (none) to 8.

settings.name: Border Colour
settings.tip: The border's colour.

settings.name: Hide With the Bars
settings.tip: The lines go when the bars pause (fullscreen, covered, Pause Visualizer), as they did. Off: only the rows below hide them.

settings.name: Hide for Fullscreen
settings.tip: The lines go while a game or video is fullscreen, whatever the bars do.

settings.name: Hide When Covered
settings.tip: The lines go while windows cover them (by the share below).

settings.name: Covered Share (%)
settings.tip: How much of the lines has to be under windows, 5 to 100 (fully hidden).

settings.name: Auto-Hide in Silence
settings.tip: The lines fade out after a stretch of silence and back when sound returns, as the bars' Auto-Hide.

settings.name: Silence Before Hiding (s)
settings.tip: Seconds of silence before they fade, 1 to 600.

settings.name: Track Progress Bar
settings.tip:
A thin bar showing how far into the song you are, near the visualizer.
Try: On with Height 2 for a subtle progress line.

settings.name: Placement
options: Inside the panel, under the bars
settings.tip:
Where the song progress bar sits.
Below the panel: under the visualizer.
Above the panel: over it.
Inside the panel, under the bars: in the panel's bottom padding.
Try: Inside the panel for a built-in look.

settings.name: Height
settings.tip:
How thick the progress bar is, in pixels.
Try: 2 for a hairline, 4 for a clear bar.

settings.name: Gap
settings.tip:
The space between the progress bar and the panel (or the bars).
Try: 3.

settings.name: Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the played part of the progress bar.
Try: #64AA89 for muted green.

settings.name: Track Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the not-yet-played part of the progress bar.
Try: #141B1E for a dark track.

settings.name: Click to Seek
settings.tip:
Lets you click or drag along the progress bar to jump in the song.
Try: On if you want a scrubber on the desktop.

settings.name: Seek App List
options: Seek, except while these apps run
Seek only while these apps run
settings.tip:
How the Seek Apps list is used.
Except: click-to-seek works unless one of those apps is running (list your games).
Only: click-to-seek works only while one of them is running.
Try: Except, listing your games, so a click in a game never skips your song.

settings.name: Seek Apps
settings.tip:
App names where click-to-seek is turned off (or only on), separated by commas.
Try: "obs64, League of Legends".

settings.name: Terminal Style
settings.tip:
The look of the Terminal shape.
Columns: each bar as a column of characters.
Waterfall: a scrolling spectrum in characters, newest line on top.
Meters: Bass, Mid, Treble and Volume as text meters.
Try: Waterfall for a hacker-screen look.

settings.name: Font
settings.tip:
The font for the Terminal shape (a fixed-width one).
Try: Scientifica or Cascadia Mono.

settings.name: Font Size
settings.tip:
The text size of the Terminal shape, which sets the size of its whole grid.
Try: 12 for a dense grid.

settings.name: Rows
settings.tip:
How many text lines tall the Terminal columns or waterfall are.
Try: 16 for a short block, 80 for a tall wall.

settings.name: Meter Width
settings.tip:
How many characters wide the Terminal meters are.
Try: 40.

settings.name: Hot Threshold (%)
settings.tip:
How high (as a percentage) a character has to be to turn the Hot Color.
Try: 75 for only the peaks to light up.

settings.name: Column Glyph
settings.tip:
The character the Terminal columns are built from.
Try: a full block for solid columns, # for classic text.

settings.name: Peak Glyph
settings.tip:
The character used for peak caps in Terminal columns.
Try: - or _.

settings.name: Waterfall Ramp
settings.tip:
The characters from quiet to loud for the Terminal waterfall.
Try: " .:-=+*#%@" for classic ASCII shading.

settings.name: Waterfall Speed
settings.tip:
How many lines per second the Terminal waterfall scrolls.
Try: 7 for slow, 20 for lively.

settings.name: Color
settings.tip:
The main text colour of the Terminal shape.
Try: #64AA89 for muted green.

settings.name: Hot Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the loudest characters in the Terminal shape.
Try: #A95D5D for a red hot zone.

settings.name: Dim Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the faintest Terminal waterfall characters.
Try: your palette red #E57474 for a two-tone screen.

settings.name: Label Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the labels on the Terminal meters.
Try: #A95D5D.

settings.name: Analysis Engine
settings.tip:
How the sound is measured.
Precision: every bar gets its own true band, sharp bass and fast treble; everything else in Analysis applies.
Classic: the old 1.4 way, 7 bands the bars blend between; softer, blobbier movement.
Try: Precision.

settings.name: Band Layout
settings.tip:
How the spectrum is cut into bars.
Frequency Scale: Bar Count bars spread over Min to Max Frequency on the Frequency Scale.
IEC 61260: the standard audio-analyzer bands (width set by Octave Fraction); Bar Count is ignored.
Musical notes: one bar per note, tuned to A4; Bar Count is ignored.
Try: Musical with 1/12 for a piano-like spectrum.

settings.name: Octave Fraction
settings.tip:
How wide each band is for the IEC and Musical layouts; narrower means more, thinner bars.
1/1: one bar per octave, about 10 bars.
1/3: the classic studio analyzer, about 30 bars.
1/6: about 60 bars.
1/12: one bar per semitone (musical note).
1/24: a quarter tone, about 240 bars.
Try: 1/3 for a studio look, 1/12 for notes.

settings.name: Min Frequency (Hz)
settings.tip:
The lowest pitch the visualizer shows (left end).
Try: 20 for deep bass, 40 to drop the rumble.

settings.name: Max Frequency (Hz)
settings.tip:
The highest pitch the visualizer shows (right end).
Try: 16000 to drop empty treble bars.

settings.name: Tuning (A4, Hz)
settings.tip:
The reference pitch for the Musical layout.
Try: 440, the standard.

settings.name: Weighting
settings.tip:
Reshapes the levels like human hearing.
Z: flat, the honest signal.
A: like the ear at quiet volume; pulls the bass way down, so mids and highs dominate.
C: like the ear at loud volume; only trims the deepest bass and highest treble.
Try: Z for an honest view, A for a treble-forward look.

settings.name: Tilt (dB per octave)
settings.tip:
Tips the spectrum up toward the treble (dB per octave), because music naturally gets quieter higher up.
0: pink noise reads flat; real music slopes down.
1.5: a typical modern mix looks level.
3 to 6: the treble lifted more and more, so hi-hats and air show strongly.
Try: 1.5 for level-looking music, 3 if the right side looks dead.

settings.name: Detector
settings.tip:
What each bar measures in its band.
RMS: the total energy of everything in the band; right for music.
Peak: only the band's loudest single pitch; jumpier, closer to how a pure tone measures.
Try: RMS for music.

settings.name: Level Reference
settings.tip:
How bar heights are scaled.
Third-octave: every band compared as if it were a standard 1/3-octave band, so heights stay the same when you change Bar Count or layout.
Band: each band's real power, so wide bars read taller than narrow ones.
Try: Third-octave.

settings.name: FFT Window
settings.tip:
A filter that decides how sharp or clean the bars look (the FFT window).
Hann: the all-round choice.
Hamming: slightly sharper peaks, a little more smearing.
Blackman-Harris: quiet details stay visible next to loud ones; peaks slightly wider.
Flat-top: exact loudness of pure tones, but blurry.
Try: Blackman-Harris for clean, separated peaks.

settings.name: Bass Detail
settings.tip:
How much extra detail is measured in the bass (extra measuring passes).
High: 3 passes; bass bars are real and separate, even at 1/12 or 1/24 octave.
Standard: 2 passes; good for most.
Off: one pass, like the classic engine; bass bars blur together.
Try: High for crisp bass bars.

settings.name: Channel
settings.tip:
Which part of the stereo sound is shown.
Mix: both channels together.
Left or Right: one channel only.
Mid: what both speakers share (vocals, bass, kick).
Side: the difference between them, showing where the stereo width is.
Try: Mix, or Side to watch the stereo width.

settings.name: Display Floor (dBFS)
settings.tip:
The quietest sound that still shows. Lower shows more detail, and more hiss.
Try: -72 for clean, -105 for every whisper.

settings.name: Display Ceiling (dBFS)
settings.tip:
The level that fills a bar completely. Lower makes bars hit the top sooner.
Try: -20 for lively bars, -35 for very full ones.

settings.name: Ballistics
settings.tip:
How bars rise and fall.
Snappy: fast up and down, punchy (the old feel).
Smooth: softer rise and fall.
Analyzer: falls at a steady 20 dB a second, like hardware analyzers.
VU: slow, averaged movement like a VU meter.
PPM EBU / PPM DIN: broadcast peak meters; jump up instantly and fall back slowly (EBU slower, DIN faster).
Custom: uses Custom Attack and Custom Release below.
Try: Snappy for punchy, Analyzer for a calm studio fall.

settings.name: Custom Attack (ms)
settings.tip:
How fast bars rise with Ballistics set to Custom, in milliseconds.
Try: 10 for instant, 50 for softer.

settings.name: Custom Release (dB/s)
settings.tip:
How fast bars fall with Ballistics set to Custom.
Try: 20 for steady, 60 for quick drops.

settings.name: Peak Hold Time (ms)
settings.tip:
How long peak caps hang before falling, in milliseconds.
Try: 500 for a classic hang, 275 for a quicker one.

settings.name: Peak Fall
settings.tip:
How peak caps drop after hanging.
Gravity: they speed up as they fall, like a dropped object; the classic analyzer look.
Linear: they fall at a steady speed.
Try: Gravity.

settings.name: Readout Content
settings.tip:
What the readout shows.
Peak frequency: the loudest pitch right now, in Hz.
Loudness: how loud it is, in LUFS (momentary, short-term and integrated, the streaming standard).
Loudness full: adds true peak, PLR (dynamics) and stereo correlation.
Both: frequency and loudness together.
Try: Loudness to see how loud a track is mastered.

settings.name: Reset Integrated Loudness On Track Change
settings.tip:
Starts the loudness reading fresh at every new song.
Try: On to measure each song on its own.

settings.name: Bass Range - Low Edge (Hz)
settings.tip:
The lowest pitch that counts as bass, for bass boost and beat detection.
Try: 20.

settings.name: Bass Range - High Edge (Hz)
settings.tip:
The highest pitch that counts as bass. Higher includes kick punch, lower only deep sub.
Try: 175 to include kicks, 100 for sub-bass only.

settings.name: Bass Gain (dB)
settings.tip:
Turns the bass bars up or down, in dB.
Try: 3 for bigger bass bars, -3 to calm them.

settings.name: Bass Attack Time (%)
settings.tip:
How fast bass bars rise compared with the rest. Under 100 is punchier.
Try: 70 for snappier kicks.

settings.name: Bass Release Time (%)
settings.tip:
How long bass bars take to fall compared with the rest. Over 100 lets bass hang.
Try: 150 for a sustained bass look.

settings.name: Bass Hit Sensitivity
settings.tip:
How big a bass jump counts as a beat for Beat Flash and Particles.
Try: 65 to catch more beats, 35 for only hard kicks.

settings.name: Bass Hit Window (ms)
settings.tip:
How far back a beat is compared to. Short catches every bump, long only real hits.
Try: 60.

settings.name: Low Zone Edge (Hz)
settings.tip:
Where the low colour zone ends, for multiband scope colours and the bass meter.
Try: 300.

settings.name: Oscilloscope Bass Focus (Hz)
settings.tip:
Shows only the bass on the Oscilloscope so a bass note holds still as clean waves. 0 shows everything.
Try: 150 with a 50 ms Time Window for a bass-only scope.

settings.name: Bass Line
settings.tip:
A separate thin lane that follows only the bass, with kicks and snares lighting up in their own colours.
Try: On with Placement Overlay for a bass pulse over the bars.

settings.name: Style
settings.tip:
The look of the bass lane.
Line: a scrolling trace, like a heart monitor.
Fill: the same history as filled columns.
Bar: one live meter that flashes on kicks and snares.
Try: Line for a heartbeat trace.

settings.name: Placement
options: Inside the bars, along the bottom
Over the whole bar block (synced with the bars)
settings.tip:
Where the bass lane sits.
Below or Above: outside the panel.
Overlay: inside the bars, along the bottom.
Cover: over the whole bar block, in step with the bars.
Try: Overlay to run it through the visualizer.

settings.name: Layer
settings.tip: Whether the bass lane is drawn over the bars, scope or wave, or behind them. Only matters where they overlap.

settings.name: Height
settings.tip:
How tall the bass lane is, in pixels.
Try: 28 for a slim lane, 60 for a bold one.

settings.name: Width
settings.tip:
How wide the bass lane is. 0 matches the bars.
Try: 0.

settings.name: Gap
settings.tip:
The space between the bass lane and the panel.
Try: 6.

settings.name: Line Thickness
settings.tip:
How thick the bass line is, in pixels (Line style).
Try: 1 for fine, 2.5 for bold.

settings.name: Offset X
settings.tip:
Slides the bass lane left (negative) or right, in pixels.
Try: small steps like 4.

settings.name: Offset Y
settings.tip:
Slides the bass lane up (negative) or down, in pixels.
Try: small steps like -4.

settings.name: Body Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the bass lane itself.
Try: your palette red #E57474.

settings.name: Kick Color
settings.tip:
The colour kicks and 808 hits flash in the bass lane.
Try: #4CE38D for green kicks.

settings.name: Snare Color
settings.tip:
The colour snares and claps flash in the bass lane.
Try: #A95D5D for muted red snares.

settings.name: Time Window (s)
settings.tip:
How many seconds of history the bass lane shows. Shorter is faster and spikier.
Try: 0.75 for quick spikes, 4 for a slow trace.

settings.name: Body Low Edge (Hz)
settings.tip:
The lowest pitch the bass lane follows.
Try: 30.

settings.name: Body High Edge (Hz)
settings.tip:
The highest pitch the bass lane follows. 120 keeps it to kick and sub; 300 adds the low end of voices.
Try: 120 for a tight bass-only lane.

settings.name: Floor (dBFS)
settings.tip:
Bass quieter than this never shows in the lane.
Try: -85.

settings.name: Depth (dB)
settings.tip:
How much loudness range the lane covers from empty to full. Smaller is more dramatic.
Try: 24 for big swings, 48 for an even line.

settings.name: Max Boost (dB)
settings.tip:
How far the lane may lift quiet bass to fill itself. 0 turns that off.
Try: 45.

settings.name: Body Release (ms)
settings.tip:
How slowly the lane falls after a loud moment.
Try: 80 for wobbly, 300 for held notes.

settings.name: Kick Sensitivity
settings.tip:
How easily a kick or 808 hit is detected. 0 turns kicks off.
Try: 75 to catch softer kicks.

settings.name: Snare Sensitivity
settings.tip:
How easily a snare or clap is detected. 0 turns snares off.
Try: 65.

settings.name: Hit Cooldown (ms)
settings.tip:
The shortest time between two hits of the same kind, so one 808 doesn't show as several.
Try: 90, or 150 for boomy tracks.

settings.name: Depth
settings.tip:
Puts the visualizer behind the person or object in your wallpaper, like a phone lock screen clock. Needs a cut-out picture.
Try: On with Auto Cut-out on.

settings.name: Behind the Depth Cut-out
settings.tip:
With Depth on, the wallpaper's subject is drawn in front of the strip or card too, not only the bars.
Try: On, with the card over a person in the wallpaper.

settings.name: Auto Cut-out
settings.tip:
Makes the cut-out picture for each wallpaper by itself, in the background, the first time it's needed.
Try: On.

settings.name: Cutter Version
settings.tip:
Which version of the background remover to install. Empty is the newest.
Try: leave empty.

settings.name: Cutter SHA-256
settings.tip:
A checksum the background remover's download must match, for safety. Empty skips the check.
Try: leave empty unless you pin a version.

settings.name: Cutter Command
settings.tip:
The command that cuts the subject out of a wallpaper.
Try: leave as it is.

settings.name: Source
settings.tip:
Where the cut-out of your wallpaper's subject comes from.
Folder: a PNG named after the wallpaper, found in the Cutout Folder or next to the wallpaper; follows wallpaper changes.
File: one cut-out image, whatever the wallpaper is.
Key: no cut-out needed; the wallpaper's plain dark (or light) background is made see-through.
Try: Folder with Auto Cut-out on.

settings.name: Cutout Folder
settings.tip:
The folder with the cut-out pictures. Empty looks next to the wallpaper.
Try: leave empty.

settings.name: Cutout File
settings.tip:
One cut-out picture to use, with Source set to File.
Try: a PNG with a transparent background.

settings.name: Fit
settings.tip:
How the cut-out sits on the screen; use the same as your wallpaper's fit in Windows.
Fill: covers the screen, cropping the edges.
Fit: all of it shows, with bars at the sides.
Stretch: pulled to the screen's shape.
Center: actual size in the middle.
Try: Fill.

settings.name: Scale (%)
settings.tip:
Nudges the cut-out's size to line up with the wallpaper.
Try: 100.

settings.name: Offset X
settings.tip:
Nudges the cut-out left (negative) or right to line up with the wallpaper.
Try: 0.

settings.name: Offset Y
settings.tip:
Nudges the cut-out up (negative) or down to line up with the wallpaper.
Try: 0.

settings.name: Key Background
settings.tip:
With Source set to Key, which background is removed.
Dark: a dark background becomes see-through.
Light: a light one does.
Try: Dark.

settings.name: Key Threshold (%)
settings.tip:
With Source set to Key, how dark (or light) counts as background.
Try: 6, raise it if a haze shows.

settings.name: Key Softness (%)
settings.tip:
With Source set to Key, how soft the cut-out's edge is.
Try: 12.

settings.name: Glass Bars
settings.tip:
Draws the bars as glass that shows your wallpaper behind them, bent like a lens and tinted with the bar colour.
Try: On with Frost 2 and Tint 0 for clear glass.

settings.name: Bend (px)
settings.tip:
How much the glass bends the wallpaper at the bar edges. 0 is flat glass.
Try: 8 for a lens, 30 for strong warping.

settings.name: Bend Style
settings.tip:
How the glass bends the wallpaper behind each bar.
Lens: the whole bar bends it, like a magnifying glass.
Edge: only a band along the edges bends it, the middle stays clear, like liquid glass.
Try: Edge for a liquid-glass rim.

settings.name: Edge Band (px)
settings.tip:
With Bend Style set to Edge, how wide the bent band is.
Try: 10.

settings.name: Edge Light (%)
settings.tip:
How bright the light along the glass edge is.
Try: 55 for a clear rim, 0 for none.

settings.name: Tint (%)
settings.tip:
How much of the bar colour tints the glass. 0 is clear, 100 is solid colour.
Try: 0 for clear, 30 for tinted glass.

settings.name: Frost (%)
settings.tip:
Blurs what the glass shows, like frosted glass.
Try: 2 for a hint, 20 for frosted.

settings.name: Line Style
settings.tip:
With Shape = Glass Frame: how the glass edge moves with the music.
Try: Mountain for one smooth swell.

settings.name: Corner Radius (%)
settings.tip:
How round the loop is: 0 square, 100 a circle on a square screen (a pill on a wide one).
Try: 12.

settings.name: Sides
settings.tip:
Where the music moves the glass; elsewhere the band rests.
Try: All the way round.

settings.name: Columns
settings.tip:
How many columns of the music run along the glass (4 to 256).
Try: 48.

settings.name: Band (px)
settings.tip:
How thick the glass band is with nothing playing.
Try: 6.

settings.name: Height (px)
settings.tip:
How far the glass rises into the screen at full volume.
Try: 120.

settings.name: Blend (%)
settings.tip:
How much the columns melt into one liquid edge: 0 steps, 100 smooth.
Try: 100.

settings.name: Inset (px)
settings.tip:
How far in from the screen's edges the loop sits.
Try: 4.

settings.name: Bend (px)
settings.tip:
How strongly the glass bends the wallpaper, pulling it in at the edge.
Try: 28.

settings.name: Edge Band (px)
settings.tip:
How wide the curved, bending part along the glass's edges is.
Try: 22.

settings.name: Edge Light (%)
settings.tip:
How bright the light along the glass's edges is.
Try: 60.

settings.name: Tint (%)
settings.tip:
How much Tint Color colours the glass.
Try: 10.

settings.name: Tint Color
settings.tip:
The glass's colour, used at Tint.
Try: #FF66EA97 for a green glass.

settings.name: Frost (%)
settings.tip:
Blurs what the glass shows.
Try: 0 for clear glass.

settings.name: Fill In Between
settings.tip: The music's levels arrive every 10 to 20 ms, less often than the screen draws. On, each frame in between moves the edge part of the way there, so rises glide instead of jumping. Adds one block of delay.

settings.name: Rise Easing (ms)
settings.tip:
How long the edge takes to rise to a new peak, so a hard hit glides up over a few frames. 0 is the old snap.
Try: 30.

settings.name: Smoothness (%)
settings.tip:
How smoothly the glass edge glides between the music's updates: 0 exact, 100 softest.
Try: 40.

settings.name: Beat Flash (%)
settings.tip:
How brightly the glass lights up on each bass hit, in Beat Flash Color (Appearance). 0 is off.
Try: 60.

settings.name: Beat Flash Color
settings.tip:
The glass's own flash colour; its alpha is how strong.
Try: #FFFFE8C0 for a warm flash.

settings.name: Beat Flash Fade (ms)
settings.tip:
How long each flash takes to fade.
Try: 300; 120 for a strobe.

settings.name: Beat Flash Fill (%)
settings.tip:
0 lights only the glass's curves and edges; 100 fills the whole body.
Try: 30.

settings.name: Peak Line (px)
settings.tip:
A line where the edge last peaked, falling as the bars' peak caps fall, in Peak Hold Cap Color. 0 is off.
Try: 2.

settings.name: Colour Mode (%)
settings.tip:
The glass tinted by Appearance's Color Mode round the loop (gradient, rainbow, by level). 0 is off.
Try: 40 with Rainbow.

settings.name: Afterimage (%)
settings.tip:
The glass the edge just left glows faintly as it falls, down to the peak line. 0 is off.
Try: 30.

settings.name: Shadow (px)
settings.tip:
A soft shadow cast from the moving edge onto the desktop, in Appearance's Shadow Color. 0 is off.
Try: 16.

settings.name: Bass Glow (%)
settings.tip:
A glow inside the glass that swells with the bass. 0 is off.
Try: 50.

settings.name: Bass Glow Color
settings.tip:
The bass glow's colour; its alpha is how strong.
Try: #FF66EA97.

settings.name: Dynamics (%)
settings.tip:
How far the glass reads the music against its own recent average, so it moves however hot the levels run. 0 is the bars' levels as they are.
Try: 70.

settings.name: Necks
settings.tip:
The glass parts round the mouse; near flyouts, menus, windows and the islands at its band it thins out and passes behind their edges.
Try: on.

settings.name: Make Way for Windows
settings.tip:
Flyouts, menus, dialogs and other windows at the band make the glass thin out and pass behind them; off, only the mouse counts. Maximized and full-screen windows never count.
Try: on.

settings.name: Mouse Clearance (px)
settings.tip:
How far the glass keeps from the mouse, so what you point at stays clickable. 0 is none.
Try: 56.

settings.name: Neck Gap (px)
settings.tip:
Clear space between the glass and what it makes way for.
Try: 8.

settings.name: Make Way for the Cut-out
settings.tip:
With Depth on, the glass parts round the cut-out's outline too.
Try: on.

settings.name: Auto Swell
settings.tip:
Each collar sized to what it wraps and wrapped all the way round; off, Neck Swell sets it and collars show near the band only.
Try: on.

settings.name: Neck Swell (px)
settings.tip:
How thick the collar that swells round each thing is. 0 is a clean gap.
Try: 12.

settings.name: Square Edge Fade (px)
settings.tip:
Near our square things (the Now Playing text's border, or its words with no border; the taskbar's islands, the Start menu, flyouts, menus, tooltips, previews and every other window) the glass grows more see-through over this distance and passes behind them where they meet, so no round collar wraps a square box. Follows them as they move. The pointer and Depth's cut-out keep their necks. 0 is a hard edge.
Try: 16.

settings.name: Square Edge Fade Strength (%)
settings.tip:
How see-through the glass is right at the box's edge: 100 gone, 50 half.
Try: 100.

settings.name: Swell Fade (%)
settings.tip:
Thins each collar toward its edge so it melts into what's round it. 0 is solid.
Try: 50.

settings.name: Swell Blend
settings.tip:
How each collar's glass mixes with what's behind it, like layer modes.
Try: Screen for a glowing swell, Multiply for a shadowed one.

settings.name: Neck Softness (px)
settings.tip:
How softly the gaps and collars flow into the band: low tight, high liquid.
Try: 18.

settings.name: Neck Speed (ms)
settings.tip:
How long the glass takes to part and flow back.
Try: 180.

settings.name: Glass Opacity (%)
settings.tip:
How much of the bent picture fills the glass's flat middle: 0 see-through (icons show), 100 filled.
Try: 0.

settings.name: Edge Glow Color
settings.tip:
The soft glow along the glass's edges; its alpha is how strong.
Try: #8066EA97 for a faint green glow.

settings.name: Highlight Color
settings.tip:
The light on the faces turned toward Light Angle; its alpha is how strong.
Try: #FFFFE8C0 for warm light.

settings.name: Edge Line Color
settings.tip:
The thin bright line along both edges; its alpha is how strong.
Try: #FFE57474.

settings.name: Edge Line Width (px)
settings.tip:
How wide the edge line is.
Try: 2.

settings.name: Light Angle
settings.tip:
Where the light comes from: 0 top, 90 right, 180 below, 270 left.
Try: 315 for top left.

settings.name: Colour Fringe (%)
settings.tip:
How far the bend splits the colours at the edge.
Try: 30 for a prism look.

settings.name: Place In
settings.tip:
Where the visualizer lives.
Desktop: on the wallpaper, behind your apps.
Taskbar: inside the taskbar; positions become percent of the taskbar.
Panel: a small window of its own that floats with your apps; drag to move, drag an edge to scale.
Try: Desktop.

settings.name: Panel Backdrop
settings.tip:
With Place In set to Panel, what's behind the visualizer in its window.
Clear: nothing.
Acrylic: frosted, blurred glass.
Mica: the softer Windows 11 tinted material.
Try: Acrylic for frosted glass.

settings.name: Panel Hotkey
settings.tip:
With Place In set to Panel, a key combo that shows or hides it.
Try: Alt+V.

settings.name: Horizontal Position
settings.tip:
Where the visualizer sits across the screen, in percent. A drag or keyboard move overrides it.
Try: 50 for centred.

settings.name: Vertical Position
settings.tip:
Where the visualizer sits down the screen, in percent. A drag or keyboard move overrides it.
Try: 88 for near the bottom.

settings.name: Monitor
settings.tip:
Which monitor the visualizer shows on (1 is the first).
Try: 1.

settings.name: Pixel Snap
settings.tip:
Keeps every edge on whole pixels so it stays sharp. Off allows in-between sizes and positions.
Try: On for crisp pixels.

settings.name: Dock To App
settings.tip:
An app the visualizer sticks to and follows around the screen.
Try: Spotify.

settings.name: Dock Side
settings.tip:
Which side of the docked app the visualizer sits on: below, above, left or right of its window.
Try: Below.

settings.name: Dock Alignment
settings.tip:
Where along that side it sits.
Start: the left (or top) end.
Centre: the middle.
End: the right (or bottom) end.
Try: Centre.

settings.name: Dock Gap
settings.tip:
The space between the docked app and the visualizer. Negative overlaps.
Try: 4.

settings.name: Dock Shift
settings.tip:
Slides the visualizer along the docked app's side.
Try: 0.

settings.name: Split Into Two Pieces
settings.tip:
Cuts the visualizer in two and moves the second half, e.g. to sit either side of centred taskbar icons.
Try: On with Split Gap 200.

settings.name: Split Point
settings.tip:
Where the cut goes, in percent along the visualizer.
Try: 50.

settings.name: Split Gap
settings.tip:
How far the second half moves along the visualizer, in pixels.
Try: the width of what sits between, like 200.

settings.name: Split Shift
settings.tip:
How far the second half moves across the visualizer, in pixels.
Try: 0.

settings.name: Enable Keyboard Move
settings.tip:
Lets you nudge the visualizer with the keyboard while holding the move keys.
Try: On.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Modifier
settings.tip:
The keys you hold while tapping a direction to move the visualizer. The keys are swallowed, so apps never get them: two-key combos (Ctrl + Alt, Alt + Shift) are safe; a single key (Ctrl, Alt) steals shortcuts like Ctrl+S.
Try: Alt + Shift.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Direction Keys
settings.tip:
Which keys move it.
Arrow Keys and WASD: both.
Arrow Keys only.
WASD only.
Try: Arrow Keys only, so WASD stays free for games.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Step
settings.tip:
How many pixels one key press moves it.
Try: 1.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Fast Step
settings.tip:
How many pixels one press moves it while holding the Fast Key.
Try: 10.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Fine Step
settings.tip:
The tiny step used while holding the Fine Key: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 or 1/16 of a pixel. Only shows as movement with Pixel Snap off.
Try: 1/4 pixel.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Fine Key
settings.tip:
The extra key held for the fine step: None, Shift, Ctrl, Alt or Win. It can't be one already used by the modifier or the Fast Key.
Try: Ctrl.

settings.name: Keyboard Move Fast Key
settings.tip:
The extra key held for the big step: Shift, Ctrl, Alt or Win, or None to turn the big step off.
Try: Shift.

settings.name: Lock everything in place
settings.tip:
Nothing of the visualizer can be dragged or resized, by mouse or Keyboard Move, over their own settings (which come back when it's off).
The lyrics keep their own Lock in Place.
Try: On once everything is where you want it.

settings.name: Enable Drag-to-Move
settings.tip:
Lets you drag the visualizer with the mouse while holding the drag key.
Try: On.

settings.name: Snap While Dragging
settings.tip:
Makes the visualizer catch on screen edges and the centre while dragging.
Try: On.

settings.name: Snap Distance
settings.tip:
How close an edge must get before it snaps, in pixels.
Try: 8.

settings.name: Drag Modifier Key
settings.tip:
The key held while dragging the visualizer.
None: just the mouse button drags it (it can then catch clicks meant for the desktop).
Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win: only drags while that key is held.
Try: None with the left button for easy moving, Ctrl to keep the desktop clickable.

settings.name: Drag Mouse Button
settings.tip:
The mouse button that drags it: left, middle or right.
Try: Left.

settings.name: Right-Click Menu
settings.tip:
How this menu opens.
Right-Click: right-click the visualizer.
Ctrl + Right-Click: only with Ctrl held, leaving a plain right-click to the desktop.
Off: never.
Try: Right-Click.

settings.name: Menu Font
settings.tip: The font of the right-click menu, the quick-settings panel and the Style Editor, by its name as Windows lists it (CozetteVector, scientifica, Consolas). Empty uses Tourne's menu font in Tourne Desktop, else Windows' own menu font. A name that isn't installed is ignored

settings.name: Panel Colours
settings.tip: The colours of the right-click menu's quick-settings panel and the Style Editor. Own uses the colours below (the Table keeps its own colours, apart from Tourne's look groups); Tourne's Menus uses Tourne Desktop's menu colours, as before

settings.name: Panel Glass
settings.tip:
The panel's ground in Tourne Desktop's menu glass, tinted with Panel Ground; frame, lines and text unchanged.
Try: On to see the wallpaper through the panel.

settings.name: Panel Ground
settings.tip: Behind everything. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Frame Band
settings.tip: The band of the frame round them. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Frame Line
settings.tip: The frame's line, and the search hint. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Lines
settings.tip: Separators and boxes. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Edges
settings.tip: Frames round values and buttons. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Text
settings.tip: Names and values. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Accent
settings.tip: What's on and what's picked. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Dim Text
settings.tip: Headings and hints. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Panel Hover
settings.tip: Under the pointer. Used with Panel Colours set to Own

settings.name: Menu Font Size
settings.tip: The size of that font, in pixels at 100% scaling (it grows with the display's scaling). 0 keeps the font's own size. Pixel fonts look sharpest at their own size or a whole multiple of it, for example 13 or 26 for Cozette

settings.name: Monitor
settings.tip: 1-based monitor index for the strip or card; 0 puts it on the visualizer's. Dragging it onto another screen sets this

settings.name: Enabled
settings.tip:
Shows a small player (buttons or a card with album art) for whatever is playing.
Try: On with Layout set to Card.

settings.name: Icon Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the play, pause, next and previous buttons.
Try: #64AA89 for muted green.

settings.name: Previous Icon Path
settings.tip:
A picture to use for the Previous button instead of the built-in one.
Try: leave empty.

settings.name: Play Icon Path
settings.tip:
A picture to use for the Play button instead of the built-in one.
Try: leave empty.

settings.name: Pause Icon Path
settings.tip:
A picture to use for the Pause button instead of the built-in one.
Try: leave empty.

settings.name: Next Icon Path
settings.tip:
A picture to use for the Next button instead of the built-in one.
Try: leave empty.

settings.name: Icon Size
settings.tip:
How big each player button is, in pixels.
Try: 16 for small, 32 for easy clicking.

settings.name: Icon Spacing
settings.tip:
The space between player buttons.
Try: 10.

settings.name: Backing Plate Color
settings.tip:
A panel behind the player buttons. Transparent means none.
Try: #141B1E for a dark plate.

settings.name: Backing Plate Padding
settings.tip:
The space between the buttons and the plate's edge.
Try: 4.

settings.name: Backing Plate Corner Radius
settings.tip:
How round the plate's corners are.
Try: 0 for square, 8 for soft.

settings.name: Backing Plate Border Size
settings.tip:
An outline around the plate. 0 is none.
Try: 1.

settings.name: Backing Plate Border Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the plate's outline.
Try: #64AA89.

settings.name: Stacking
options: Always on top (covers apps, even ones run as administrator)
Normal window (apps you click on cover it)
settings.tip:
Whether the player stays above other windows.
Always on top: covers apps, even admin ones.
Normal window: apps you click on cover it.
Try: Always on top with Hide When Covered on.

settings.name: Hide When Covered
settings.tip:
Hides the player while a window sits over it.
Try: On.

settings.name: Hide When Covered - Threshold
settings.tip:
How much of the player has to be under a window before it hides: from 5% (hides as soon as a window touches it) to 100% (only when fully covered).
Try: 50.

settings.name: Horizontal Position
settings.tip:
Where the player sits across the screen, in percent.
Try: 50.

settings.name: Vertical Position
settings.tip:
Where the player sits down the screen, in percent.
Try: 95.

settings.name: Anchor
settings.tip:
Where the player is placed.
Screen: by the Horizontal and Vertical Position percentages.
Panel corners: pinned inside that corner of the visualizer's panel, moving with it.
Try: Panel, top right, to keep it with the visualizer.

settings.name: Anchor Inset X
settings.tip:
How far in from the panel's side the pinned player sits.
Try: 8.

settings.name: Anchor Inset Y
settings.tip:
How far in from the panel's top or bottom the pinned player sits.
Try: 8.

settings.name: Layout
settings.tip:
What kind of player it is.
Strip: just previous, play/pause and next.
Card: a small card with album art, title, a seek bar, an output switch and volume.
Try: Card.

settings.name: Card Background
settings.tip:
The card's fill colour.
Try: #121C21 for your dark ground.

settings.name: Card Border Color
settings.tip:
The colour of the card's border.
Try: #64AA89.

settings.name: Card Border Size
settings.tip:
How thick the card's border is.
Try: 1.

settings.name: Card Corner Radius
settings.tip:
How round the card's corners are. One number, or four for each corner.
Try: 0 for square, 12 for soft.

settings.name: Card Art Corner Radius
settings.tip:
How round the album art's corners are. -1 follows the card.
Try: -1.

settings.name: Card Art Size
settings.tip:
How wide the album art is, which sets the card's width. 0 sizes it from the icons.
Try: 150.

settings.name: Card Art Height
settings.tip:
How tall the card's art (or what's in its place) is. 0 keeps it square. Dragging the card's top or bottom edge sets it.
Try: 0 for square art, 60 for a short wide banner.

settings.name: Card Art Padding
settings.tip:
Room around the card's art at the top and sides, apart from the rest of the card's padding. -1 uses the card's padding; 0 runs the art to the card's edges.
Try: 0 for an edge-to-edge cover, 4 for a thin frame.

settings.name: Card Art Gap
settings.tip:
Room between the art and the title (or seek bar) under it. -1 keeps the usual gap.
Try: 2 to tuck the title up under the art, 12 to give it air.

settings.name: In the Art's Place
settings.tip:
What the top of the card shows.
Album art: the song's cover.
Nothing: no art, just a slim row of buttons, so the card is only text and controls.
Mini visualizer: the Table's bars drawn small, in your colours.
Big type: the title as large as it fits, artist under it.
Colour block: the cover's main colours as stripes, no picture.
Player badge: the playing app's icon and name.
Clock: the time, with the time left in the song.
Try: Mini visualizer for a card that dances, Colour block for a calm swatch.

settings.name: Card Accent
settings.tip:
The colour of the card's seek bar, volume bar and their knobs.
Icon Color: same as the icons.
Card Accent Color: the colour you set below.
Album art: the cover's main colour, changing with each song.
Windows accent: your Windows accent colour.
Try: Album art so the card matches each song.

settings.name: Card Accent Color
settings.tip:
The seek and volume colour, with Card Accent set to a custom colour.
Try: #E57474.

settings.name: Card Track Title
settings.tip:
What text shows under the art.
Title and artist.
Title only.
Off: no text, a smaller card.
Try: Title and artist.

settings.name: Card Title Scrolling
settings.tip:
What a title too long for the card does.
Scroll on hover: scrolls while your pointer is over the card, otherwise fades at the end.
Always scroll: keeps scrolling.
Never scroll: just fades at the end.
Try: Scroll on hover.
